newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mondragon sees 1996 net at 430 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Mondragon sees 1996 net at 430 mln pesos.

text.p: Mondragon International Phils Inc said on Friday its preliminary figures indictated net profit in 1996 would reach 430 million pesos compared with the audited figure of 216 million pesos in 1995.
The firm also said in a statement it expects to make a net profit of 650 million pesos this year.
The estimated net profits of over 500 million pesos from Mondragon's casino unit offset the firm's losses from consumer distribution in 1996, the statement said.

Earlier, the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) denied a request by Mondragon to suspend trading of its shares due to Mondragon's dispute with the state-run Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp (Pagcor) .

Mondragon was granted a permit by Pagcor in 1995 to operate an unlimited number of casinos at the Clark Special Economic Zone, north of Manila. Pagcor, which also operates a nearby casino, has accused Mondragon of violations of the permit.

"We are well aware that the main reason for the strong showing of Mondragon has been the anticipated results of our casino operations. Therefore, we seek your consent to the request," Mondragon chairman Jose Antonio Gonzalez told the bourse in a statement.
"With respect to the request for voluntary suspension from trading, the exchange deems it proper to allow the trading of the securities to continue," the PSE said.
